records.source: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ κατὰ τὴν οὖσαν ἐκκλησίαν προφῆται καὶ διδάσκαλοι ὅ τε Βαρναβᾶς καὶ Συμεὼν ὁ καλούμενος Νίγερ, καὶ Λούκιος ὁ Κυρηναῖος, Μαναήν τε Ἡρῴδου τοῦ τετραάρχου σύντροφος καὶ Σαῦλος.
records.gloss: There were now in Antioch in the being [there] church prophets and teachers, both Barnabas and Simeon the [one] being called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen also, of Herod the tetrarch brought up with, and Saul.
pieces: The church in Antioch had prophets and teachers among its members: Barnabas, Simeon known as Niger, Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen, a childhood companion of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

L.1: Now there were in Antioch, in the church that was [there], prophets and teachers: both Barnabas and Simeon, who was called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaen, brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

R.1: The church in the city of Antioch had some prophets and teachers. They were Barnabas, Simeon (who was also called Niger), Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen, and Saul. Manaen had grown up with Herod, the ruler of Galilee.

decisions.choice: Herod the tetrarch: Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: Luke uses the title tetrarch for Herod Antipas, who ruled Galilee in Jesus's day (Luke 3:1, 3:19, 9:7). Agrippa, who died in 12:23, was a king.

decisions.choice: brought up with: raised together with, a childhood companion or foster brother
decisions.reason: The word means one reared alongside another. It was also used as an honorary title at royal courts, but here it most likely means Manaen grew up with Antipas.

decisions.choice: Niger: a Latin name meaning "black"
decisions.reason: It is a common Latin surname. Lucius comes from Cyrene in North Africa, from where some of the first preachers to Gentiles in Antioch had come (11:20).

decisions.choice: prophets and teachers: the five are named as one group
alternatives: the first three as prophets, the last two as teachers
decisions.reason: The way the Greek joins the names may hint at two groups, but Luke does not say who was which.

decisions.choice: Manaen had grown up with Herod, the ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title, as the meaning note does, and moves the fact about Manaen into its own sentence.

records.heading: The Spirit sets apart Barnabas and Saul

records.source: λειτουργούντων δὲ αὐτῶν τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ νηστευόντων εἶπεν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον· Ἀφορίσατε δή μοι τὸν Βαρναβᾶν καὶ Σαῦλον εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ προσκέκλημαι αὐτούς.
records.gloss: As were ministering now they to the Lord and fasting, said the Spirit the Holy, Set apart then to me the Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.
pieces: While they were serving the Lord in worship and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set Barnabas and Saul apart for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for the work I have called them to do."

L.2: Now as they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart now for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."

R.2: One day they were worshiping the Lord and fasting. Then the Holy Spirit spoke to them: "Set Barnabas and Saul apart for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I have called them to do a special work."

decisions.choice: ministering: serving the Lord in worship and prayer
decisions.reason: The word was used of priests serving in the temple (Luke 1:23, Hebrews 10:11). Here it describes the church's worship.

decisions.choice: they: the prophets and teachers, and perhaps the whole church
decisions.reason: The pronoun most naturally points back to the five named in 13:1. Luke does not say whether the rest of the church was there.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit speaks as a person and claims the two for himself
decisions.reason: The Spirit says "for me" and "I have called them". Luke does not say how the Spirit spoke; it may have been through one of the prophets.

decisions.choice: a special work
decisions.reason: Readable adds "special" to show that a particular task is meant; Luke tells what it was in the chapters that follow.

records.source: τότε νηστεύσαντες καὶ προσευξάμενοι καὶ ἐπιθέντες τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἀπέλυσαν.
records.gloss: Then having fasted and having prayed and having laid the hands on them they sent [them] off.
pieces: Then, after more fasting and prayer, they laid their hands on the two men and let them go.

L.3: Then, having fasted and prayed and laid [their] hands on them, they sent [them] off.

R.3: So the church fasted and prayed again. They put their hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them on their way.

decisions.choice: laying on of hands: a sign of blessing and of handing over a task
alternatives: giving them a rank they did not have
decisions.reason: The same act marked the Seven for their work (6:6). Paul and Barnabas later report back to this church about the work it had committed them to (14:26).

decisions.choice: sent off: released them, let them go
decisions.reason: The verb means to release or dismiss. The next verse says it was the Holy Spirit who sent them.

decisions.choice: the church ... again
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, since the sentence carries on from 13:2, and says the fasting continued.

records.source: Αὐτοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐκπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος κατῆλθον εἰς Σελεύκειαν, ἐκεῖθέν τε ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Κύπρον, καὶ γενόμενοι ἐν Σαλαμῖνι κατήγγελλον τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· εἶχον δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννην ὑπηρέτην.
records.gloss: They indeed therefore having been sent forth by the Holy Spirit went down to Seleucia, from there then they sailed to Cyprus, \v 5 and having come into Salamis they were proclaiming the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews; they had now also John [as] a helper.
pieces: So, sent out by the Holy Spirit, the two went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus.
Arriving at Salamis, they began to proclaim the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. They also had John with them as an assistant.

L.4: So they, having been sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus.
L.5: And having arrived in Salamis, they were proclaiming the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews; and they also had John [as their] helper.

R.4: The Holy Spirit sent Barnabas and Saul out. They went down to the port of Seleucia, and from there they sailed to the island of Cyprus.
R.5: When they came to the town of Salamis, they told people the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. John Mark was with them to help them.

decisions.choice: Seleucia, Cyprus, Salamis: the port of Antioch, the island, and its chief eastern town
decisions.reason: Seleucia was the seaport of Syrian Antioch. Barnabas came from Cyprus (4:36), and believers from Cyprus had preached in Antioch (11:20). Salamis lay on the island's east coast.

decisions.choice: they were proclaiming: they set about preaching, from synagogue to synagogue
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures an ongoing activity. Going first to the synagogue becomes Paul's pattern (13:14, 14:1, 17:1-2).

decisions.choice: John: John Mark, as their assistant
decisions.reason: John called Mark came with Barnabas and Saul from Jerusalem (12:12, 12:25). The word for helper means an assistant or attendant.

decisions.choice: the port of, the island of, the town of; John Mark
decisions.reason: Readable says what each place was and gives John his other name, as the meaning notes explain.

records.heading: The proconsul and the magician on Cyprus

records.source: διελθόντες δὲ ὅλην τὴν νῆσον ἄχρι Πάφου εὗρον ἄνδρα τινὰ μάγον ψευδοπροφήτην Ἰουδαῖον ᾧ ὄνομα Βαριησοῦ, ὃς ἦν σὺν τῷ ἀνθυπάτῳ Σεργίῳ Παύλῳ, ἀνδρὶ συνετῷ.
records.gloss: Having passed through now all the island as far as Paphos they found a man certain, a magician, a false prophet, Jewish, whose name [was] Bar-Jesus, \v 7 who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a man intelligent.
pieces: They went across the whole island as far as Paphos, and there they came upon a Jewish magician, a false prophet, whose name was Bar-Jesus.
He was in the company of the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding.

L.6: And having gone through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a Jewish false prophet, whose name [was] Bar-Jesus,
L.7: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man.

R.6: They traveled across the whole island to the city of Paphos. There they met a Jewish man named Bar-Jesus. He practiced magic and claimed to be a prophet, but he was a false prophet.
R.7: He was one of the people around Sergius Paulus, the Roman governor of the island. Sergius Paulus was a wise man.

decisions.choice: magician: one who claimed secret knowledge and powers
alternatives: a wise man from the East, as in Matthew 2:1
decisions.reason: The same word names the visitors in Matthew 2:1, but here, joined with "false prophet", it describes a man who practiced magic, like Simon in 8:9.

decisions.choice: Bar-Jesus: "son of Jesus", that is, son of Joshua
decisions.reason: Bar means son in Aramaic, and Jesus was a common Jewish name. Paul will call him "son of the devil" (13:10).

decisions.choice: proconsul: the Roman governor of a province ruled by the Senate
decisions.reason: Cyprus was a senatorial province, governed by a proconsul, in this period. Luke uses the correct title. Paphos, on the west coast, was the seat of government.

decisions.choice: who was with the proconsul: one of his circle, an adviser or attendant
decisions.reason: The phrase describes a lasting connection. Roman officials sometimes kept advisers who claimed to read the future.

decisions.choice: he practiced magic and claimed to be a prophet; the Roman governor of the island
alternatives: a magician, a false prophet; the proconsul
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two words and the title, as the meaning notes do.

records.source: οὗτος προσκαλεσάμενος Βαρναβᾶν καὶ Σαῦλον ἐπεζήτησεν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: This [man] having called to [him] Barnabas and Saul desired to hear the word of God;
pieces: The proconsul sent for Barnabas and Saul and asked to hear the word of God.

L.7: This [man], having summoned Barnabas and Saul, sought to hear the word of God.

R.7: Sergius Paulus asked Barnabas and Saul to come to him. He wanted to hear the word of God.

decisions.choice: this man: the proconsul, not the magician
decisions.reason: The last person named is Sergius Paulus, and the next verse sets the magician against him and his wish to hear.

decisions.choice: sought: wanted earnestly, asked
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek with intent or desire.

decisions.choice: the proconsul (B); Sergius Paulus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the man, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ἀνθίστατο δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἐλύμας ὁ μάγος, οὕτως γὰρ μεθερμηνεύεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, ζητῶν διαστρέψαι τὸν ἀνθύπατον ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως.
records.gloss: Was opposing however them Elymas the magician, thus for is translated the name of him, seeking to turn away the proconsul from the faith.
pieces: But the magician Elymas, for that is how his name is translated, kept opposing them and tried to steer the proconsul away from the faith.

L.8: But Elymas the magician (for so his name is translated) was opposing them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

R.8: But the magician fought against them. (His name, Elymas, means "magician".) He tried to stop the governor from putting his faith in Jesus.

decisions.choice: Elymas: another name, which Luke explains as meaning "magician"
decisions.reason: Elymas does not translate Bar-Jesus. Luke most likely means that Elymas is a word for magician or sorcerer, perhaps from a Semitic word for a wise man. The origin of the name is not certain.

decisions.choice: the faith: believing the message about Jesus
alternatives: the Christian teaching as a body of belief
decisions.reason: The proconsul was coming to believe (13:12). "The faith" here is that trust, which Elymas tried to prevent.

decisions.choice: was opposing: kept opposing them
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures continued resistance.

decisions.choice: his name as an aside in parentheses; putting his faith in Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable sets the note about the name apart and says what the faith was, as the meaning notes explain.

records.source: Σαῦλος δέ, ὁ καὶ Παῦλος, πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Ὦ πλήρης παντὸς δόλου καὶ πάσης ῥᾳδιουργίας, υἱὲ διαβόλου, ἐχθρὲ πάσης δικαιοσύνης, οὐ παύσῃ διαστρέφων τὰς ὁδοὺς κυρίου τὰς εὐθείας;
records.gloss: Saul then, the [one] also [called] Paul, having been filled [with the] Holy Spirit, having looked intently upon him \v 10 said, O full of all deceit and all fraud, son of [the] devil, enemy of all righteousness, not will you cease perverting the ways of [the] Lord the straight?
pieces: Then Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fixed his eyes on him
and said, "You are full of every kind of deceit and villainy, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness! Will you never stop twisting the straight paths of the Lord?

L.9: But Saul, who [is] also [called] Paul, filled with [the] Holy Spirit, looked intently at him
L.10: [and] said, "O full of all deceit and all fraud, son of [the] devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop perverting the straight ways of [the] Lord?

R.9: Saul's other name was Paul. Now Paul was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
R.10: and said, "You are full of lies and tricks! You are a son of the devil! You are an enemy of all righteousness! You keep trying to make the Lord's straight paths crooked. Will you never stop?

decisions.choice: Saul, who is also Paul: one man with two names
decisions.reason: Many Jews of the time had a Jewish name and a Greek or Roman one. Paul is a Roman name. From here on Luke calls him Paul, as he begins to work among Gentiles; Luke does not say he took the name at this moment.

decisions.choice: son of the devil: one who acts like the devil and serves him
decisions.reason: "Son of" means one who shares another's character (John 8:44). It answers his name Bar-Jesus, "son of Jesus" (13:6).

decisions.choice: righteousness: what is right in God's sight
decisions.reason: He opposes everything that is right and good before God.

decisions.choice: the straight ways of the Lord: the right paths God has made
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of the Lord's ways as straight and right (Hosea 14:9). Elymas twists them, by turning the proconsul from the truth. The Hebrew of such passages has the divine name.

decisions.choice: You keep trying to make the Lord's straight paths crooked. Will you never stop?
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question to make the picture clear.

records.source: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ χεὶρ κυρίου ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ ἔσῃ τυφλὸς μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον ἄχρι καιροῦ.
records.gloss: And now behold, [the] hand of [the] Lord [is] upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a season.
pieces: Now look: the hand of the Lord is against you. You will be blind and unable to see the sun for a while."

L.11: And now look, [the] hand of [the] Lord [is] upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time."

R.11: Now the Lord is going to punish you. You will be blind. For a while you will not even be able to see the sun."

decisions.choice: the hand of the Lord upon you: the Lord acting against you in judgment
decisions.reason: The hand of the Lord can bring help (11:21) or punishment (1 Samuel 5:6, Exodus 9:3). Here it brings blindness.

decisions.choice: for a time: the blindness will not last for ever
decisions.reason: The phrase means until a set time. The judgment leaves room for mercy, as Saul's own blindness did (9:8-9, 9:18).

decisions.choice: the Lord is going to punish you
alternatives: the hand of the Lord is upon you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: παραχρῆμα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀχλὺς καὶ σκότος, καὶ περιάγων ἐζήτει χειραγωγούς.
records.gloss: Immediately then fell upon him mist and darkness, and going about he was seeking people to lead [him] by the hand.
pieces: At once a mist and a darkness came down on him, and he moved about looking for someone to lead him by the hand.

L.11: And immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and going about he was seeking people to lead [him] by the hand.

R.11: Right away his eyes became misty and dark. He walked around trying to find someone to hold his hand and lead him.

decisions.choice: mist: a clouding of the eyes
decisions.reason: The word was used by Greek doctors for a clouding of the eye. With darkness, it describes his sight failing.

decisions.choice: he was seeking: he kept groping about for a guide
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures him searching, as Saul himself had once been led by the hand (9:8).

decisions.choice: his eyes became misty and dark
alternatives: mist and darkness fell on him
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the darkness was in his eyes, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: τότε ἰδὼν ὁ ἀνθύπατος τὸ γεγονὸς ἐπίστευσεν ἐκπλησσόμενος ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ τοῦ κυρίου.
records.gloss: Then having seen the proconsul the [thing] having happened believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
pieces: The proconsul, seeing what had taken place, believed. He was struck with amazement at the teaching about the Lord.

L.12: Then the proconsul, having seen what had happened, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

R.12: When the governor saw what had happened, he believed. The teaching about the Lord Jesus amazed him.

decisions.choice: the teaching of the Lord: the teaching about the Lord
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean either. Paul and Barnabas were proclaiming the message about Jesus; the teaching, more than the miracle, is what astonished him.

decisions.choice: believed: he came to believe the message
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same verb for coming to faith throughout Acts (4:4, 13:48). He does not say whether the proconsul was baptized.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the Lord, as 13:8 and 13:38-39 make clear.

records.source: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Πάφου οἱ περὶ Παῦλον ἦλθον εἰς Πέργην τῆς Παμφυλίας· Ἰωάννης δὲ ἀποχωρήσας ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
records.gloss: Having sailed then from Paphos those around Paul came to Perga of Pamphylia; John however having departed from them returned to Jerusalem.
pieces: Paul and those with him put out to sea from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them there and went back to Jerusalem.

L.13: Then, having put out to sea from Paphos, those around Paul came to Perga in Pamphylia; but John, leaving them, returned to Jerusalem.

R.13: Paul and his friends left Paphos by ship. They came to the town of Perga in the region of Pamphylia. But John Mark left them there and went home to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: those around Paul: Paul and his companions
decisions.reason: From here Luke usually names Paul first (13:43, 13:46), as the leader in speaking.

decisions.choice: Perga of Pamphylia: a city near the south coast of Asia Minor
decisions.reason: Pamphylia was a region on the southern coast of what is now Turkey.

decisions.choice: departed: withdrew from them
decisions.reason: Luke does not give his reason. Paul later refused to take him again because he had left them (15:38).

decisions.choice: the town of, the region of; John Mark
decisions.reason: Readable says what the places were and names John as in 13:5.

records.heading: Paul speaks in the synagogue at Antioch

records.source: αὐτοὶ δὲ διελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Πέργης παρεγένοντο εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν τὴν Πισιδίαν, καὶ εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐκάθισαν.
records.gloss: They now having passed through from Perga came to Antioch the Pisidian, and having gone into the synagogue on the day of the Sabbaths they sat down.
pieces: They went on from Perga and arrived at Antioch near Pisidia. On the Sabbath day they went into the synagogue and took their seats.

L.14: And they, having gone on from Perga, came to Pisidian Antioch, and going into the synagogue on the day of the Sabbath, they sat down.

R.14: From Perga they traveled inland to the city of Antioch, near the region of Pisidia. On the Sabbath day they went into the synagogue and sat down.

decisions.choice: Pisidian Antioch: the Antioch toward Pisidia, a Roman colony inland
decisions.reason: This is not the Antioch of 13:1. This city lay in the province of Galatia, in Phrygia, near the border of Pisidia, which is why it was called Pisidian Antioch.

decisions.choice: they sat down: they joined the synagogue meeting
decisions.reason: Visitors sat among the congregation. In 13:15 the leaders invite them to speak.

decisions.choice: Antioch near Pisidia
decisions.reason: The city was close to Pisidia rather than in it, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps the Greek description.

records.source: μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγοντες· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, εἴ τίς ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν λόγος παρακλήσεως πρὸς τὸν λαόν, λέγετε.
records.gloss: After then the reading of the law and of the prophets sent the synagogue rulers to them saying, Men brothers, if any is among you word of exhortation toward the people, speak.
pieces: When the Law and the Prophets had been read, the leaders of the synagogue sent a message to them: "Brothers, if one of you has a word of encouragement for the people, speak."

L.15: And after the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, "Men, brothers, if there is among you any word of exhortation for the people, speak."

R.15: First, some parts of God's law and of the books of the prophets were read aloud. Then the leaders of the synagogue sent someone to say to Paul and Barnabas, "Brothers, if you have anything to say that will encourage the people, please tell us."

decisions.choice: the reading of the Law and the Prophets: the readings of a synagogue service
decisions.reason: A passage from the law of Moses was read, and then one from the Prophets (Luke 4:16-17). Visitors might then be asked to speak.

decisions.choice: rulers of the synagogue: the leaders in charge of the meeting
decisions.reason: They chose who would read and speak (Luke 8:41, 13:14).

decisions.choice: men, brothers: a courteous address to fellow Jews, here to Paul and his companions
decisions.reason: The rulers speak to the visiting men. As a group of named men is meant, the address does not include women here.

decisions.choice: word of exhortation: a message of encouragement and appeal
decisions.reason: The word covers both encouragement and urging. Hebrews calls itself a word of exhortation (Hebrews 13:22).

decisions.choice: Brothers, with no setting
decisions.reason: The rulers speak to the men who came with Paul, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps "Men, brothers".

decisions.choice: some parts of God's law and of the books of the prophets were read aloud
alternatives: after the reading of the Law and the Prophets
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the reading was.

records.source: ἀναστὰς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ κατασείσας τῇ χειρὶ εἶπεν· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν, ἀκούσατε.
records.gloss: Having risen then Paul and having motioned with the hand said, Men Israelites and those fearing God, listen.
pieces: Paul stood up, waved his hand for quiet, and said, "{{gender:People|Men}} of Israel, and you God-fearing Gentiles, listen.

L.16: Then Paul stood up, and motioning with [his] hand said, "Men, Israelites, and those who fear God, listen.

R.16: So Paul stood up. He raised his hand to ask them to be quiet. Then he said, "People of Israel, and you other people here who worship God, listen to me!

decisions.choice: men, Israelites: a formal address to the Jews in the synagogue
decisions.reason: Speeches in Acts open this way (2:22, 3:12). Women were present in synagogue meetings, and women of the city are named in 13:50, so the address most likely takes in the whole congregation; the words alone cannot settle it.

decisions.choice: those who fear God: Gentiles who worshiped the God of Israel without becoming Jews
decisions.reason: Luke uses this phrase for Gentiles like Cornelius (10:2, 10:22). Here they are set beside the Israelites, and again in 13:26.

decisions.choice: motioning with his hand: a speaker's gesture for silence
decisions.reason: Peter and Paul do the same before speaking (12:17, 21:40).

decisions.choice: People of Israel, with "Men of Israel" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The inclusive default follows the meaning note; Literal keeps "men".

decisions.choice: you God-fearing Gentiles
decisions.reason: Balanced names the group, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps the phrase.

decisions.choice: you other people here who worship God
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that these hearers are not Israelites and that they worship God.

records.source: ὁ θεὸς τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου Ἰσραὴλ ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν, καὶ τὸν λαὸν ὕψωσεν ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ μετὰ βραχίονος ὑψηλοῦ ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ἐξ αὐτῆς, καί, ὡς τεσσερακονταετῆ χρόνον ἐτροποφόρησεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, καὶ καθελὼν ἔθνη ἑπτὰ ἐν γῇ Χανάαν κατεκληρονόμησεν τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα.
records.gloss: The God of the people this Israel chose the fathers of us, and the people exalted in the sojourn in [the] land of Egypt, and with arm uplifted brought them out of it, \v 18 and of about forty years [a] period he endured the ways of them in the wilderness, \v 19 and having destroyed nations seven in [the] land of Canaan he gave as inheritance the land of them \v 20 for about years four hundred and fifty.
pieces: The God of this people Israel chose our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. During their stay as foreigners in the land of Egypt {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the people great, and with a raised arm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them out of that land.
For about forty years {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bore with their ways in the desert,
and after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave their land to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people to possess.
The whole span was about 450 years.

L.17: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and made the people great during [their] stay as foreigners in [the] land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them out of it.
L.18: And for a period of about forty years {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put up with them in the wilderness.
L.19: And having destroyed seven nations in [the] land of Canaan, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave [them] their land as an inheritance,

R.17: The God of the people of Israel chose our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. While they were living in Egypt as foreigners, God made them a great people. Then by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out of Egypt.
R.18: For about forty years {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was patient with them in the desert.
R.19: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave their land to Israel to keep.
R.20: All of this happened over about 450 years.

decisions.choice: with an uplifted arm: by God's mighty power, as in the Exodus
decisions.reason: The Old Testament describes the Exodus with these words (Exodus 6:1, 6:6; Deuteronomy 5:15). An arm raised high is a picture of strength.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "he put up with their ways"
alternatives: "he cared for them", "he carried them like a nurse"
decisions.reason: The two Greek verbs differ by one letter. Some important manuscripts read the word for carrying and caring for them, which is the reading of the Greek Old Testament in Deuteronomy 1:31. Others, followed by the SBLGNT, read the word for bearing with someone's ways. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: seven nations: the peoples of Canaan
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 7:1 names the seven nations that God would drive out before Israel.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: about 450 years belongs with what comes before
alternatives: about 450 years belongs to the time of the judges
decisions.reason: In the SBLGNT the 450 years close the sentence about Egypt, the wilderness and the land, and 13:20 goes on, "And after these things he gave judges". Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, put the words after "these things", so that the judges ruled about 450 years. On the SBLGNT reading the figure most likely covers the stay in Egypt (about 400 years, 7:6), the forty years in the wilderness and the conquest. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: sojourn: living in a land as foreigners
decisions.reason: The word means a stay in a land that is not one's own, as in 7:6.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means forebears; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: by his great power
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: a separate sentence for the 450 years
alternatives: for about 450 years, joined to the giving of the land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set the figure apart so that it is clear it sums up the whole period described, as the SBLGNT punctuation has it.

records.source: καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἔδωκεν κριτὰς ἕως Σαμουὴλ τοῦ προφήτου.
records.gloss: And after these things he gave [them] judges until Samuel the prophet.
pieces: After that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them judges until the time of the prophet Samuel.

L.20: And after these things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave [them] judges until Samuel the prophet.

R.20: After that, God gave them leaders called judges. They led Israel until the time of Samuel the prophet.

decisions.choice: judges: leaders God raised up to rescue and rule Israel
decisions.reason: These are the leaders of the book of Judges, such as Gideon and Deborah (Judges 2:16). Samuel was the last of them (1 Samuel 7:15).

decisions.choice: leaders called judges. They led Israel
decisions.reason: Readable explains what kind of judges these were.

records.source: κἀκεῖθεν ᾐτήσαντο βασιλέα, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς τὸν Σαοὺλ υἱὸν Κίς, ἄνδρα ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμίν, ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα·
records.gloss: And then they asked for a king, and gave them God Saul son of Kish, a man of tribe of Benjamin, years forty;
pieces: Next they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who reigned forty years.

L.21: And then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man of [the] tribe of Benjamin, [for] forty years.

R.21: Then the people asked God for a king. So God gave them Saul, the son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin. Saul was king for forty years.

decisions.choice: forty years: the length of Saul's reign
alternatives: the length of Samuel's and Saul's time together
decisions.reason: The Old Testament does not state the length of Saul's reign clearly; the number in 1 Samuel 13:1 is damaged in the Hebrew. Josephus also gives forty years in one place (Antiquities 6.378).

decisions.choice: Saul son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin: the first king of Israel
decisions.reason: The story is told in 1 Samuel 8-10. Paul, who now speaks, also bore the name Saul and was of the tribe of Benjamin (Philippians 3:5).

decisions.choice: who reigned (B); Saul was king (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the forty years measure.

records.source: καὶ μεταστήσας αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν τὸν Δαυὶδ αὐτοῖς εἰς βασιλέα, ᾧ καὶ εἶπεν μαρτυρήσας· Εὗρον Δαυὶδ τὸν τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μου, ὃς ποιήσει πάντα τὰ θελήματά μου.
records.gloss: And having removed him he raised up David to them as king, to whom also he said having testified, I have found David the [son] of Jesse, a man according to the heart of me, who will do all the wishes of me.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had set Saul aside, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised up David to be their king, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave this testimony about him: 'I have found David son of Jesse, a man in tune with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart, who will carry out all that I want.'

L.22: And having removed him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised up David as king for them, of whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also said, bearing witness, 'I have found David the [son] of Jesse, a man according to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart, who will do all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} will.'

R.22: Later God took Saul off the throne and made David their king. This is what God said about David: 'I have found David, the son of Jesse. He is a man who wants what I want. He will do everything I want him to do.'

decisions.choice: a quotation joined from several passages
decisions.reason: "I have found David" is from Psalm 89:21; "a man after my heart" from 1 Samuel 13:14; "who will do all my will" recalls Isaiah 44:28. Paul joins them into one testimony about David.

decisions.choice: a man according to my heart: a man of God's own choosing, whose will agrees with God's
alternatives: a man with a warm heart
decisions.reason: In 1 Samuel 13:14 the phrase speaks of the man God has chosen, set against Saul who disobeyed.

decisions.choice: removed: set aside as king
decisions.reason: God rejected Saul as king (1 Samuel 15:23, 16:1). The word means to remove from a position.

decisions.choice: a man who wants what I want
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: τούτου ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος κατ’ ἐπαγγελίαν ἤγαγεν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ σωτῆρα Ἰησοῦν, προκηρύξαντος Ἰωάννου πρὸ προσώπου τῆς εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ βάπτισμα μετανοίας παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: Of this [man] God from the seed according to promise has brought to Israel a Savior Jesus, \v 24 having proclaimed beforehand John before [the] face of the coming of him a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
pieces: From this man's line God has brought Israel a Savior, Jesus, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised.
Before Jesus came, John had proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

L.23: From the seed of this [man] God, according to [the] promise, has brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus,
L.24: after John had proclaimed before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

R.23: God promised that the Savior would come from David's family. And God kept that promise. He sent Jesus to Israel to save them.
R.24: Before Jesus came, John told all the people of Israel that they must turn away from their sins and be baptized.

decisions.choice: according to promise: God's promise of a son of David to reign
decisions.reason: God promised David a descendant whose kingdom would last for ever (2 Samuel 7:12-16; Luke 1:32-33, 1:69).

decisions.choice: Savior: the one who rescues and brings salvation
decisions.reason: The same title as in 5:31 and Luke 2:11. The message of salvation follows in 13:26.

decisions.choice: before the face of his coming: before he came
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying "before". It refers to Jesus beginning his work.

decisions.choice: a baptism of repentance: baptism that showed people were turning from their sins
decisions.reason: As in Luke 3:3. Repentance means a change of mind and life.

decisions.choice: the promise first, then God sending Jesus, in three sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence and says what the promise was, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: to save them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title Savior.

records.source: ὡς δὲ ἐπλήρου Ἰωάννης τὸν δρόμον, ἔλεγεν· Τί ἐμὲ ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι;
records.gloss: As then was fulfilling John the course, he was saying, What me do you suppose to be?
pieces: As John was finishing his course, he kept saying, 'Who do you think I am?

L.25: And as John was completing [his] course, he was saying, 'What do you suppose me to be?

R.25: When John's work was nearly finished, he said to the people, 'Who do you think I am?

decisions.choice: fulfilling the course: completing his life's work
decisions.reason: The word means a race or course run. Paul uses the same picture of his own work (20:24, 2 Timothy 4:7).

decisions.choice: he was saying: he said it more than once
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense suggests a saying John repeated. The Gospels report it in several forms (Luke 3:15-16, John 1:20, 1:27).

decisions.choice: when John's work was nearly finished
alternatives: as John was completing his course
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγώ· ἀλλ’ ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετ’ ἐμὲ οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν λῦσαι.
records.gloss: Not am I [he]; but behold, comes after me [one] of whom not I am worthy the sandal of the feet to untie.
pieces: I am not the one. No, someone is coming after me, and I am not fit to untie the sandal on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.'

L.25: I am not [he]. But look, [one] is coming after me, the sandal of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.'

R.25: I am not the Savior you are waiting for. Someone greater is coming after me. I am not good enough even to untie {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.'

decisions.choice: I am not he: I am not the one you are expecting, the Messiah
decisions.reason: The people wondered whether John was the Messiah (Luke 3:15). John 1:20 has him say it in so many words.

decisions.choice: untie the sandal: the lowest task of a slave
decisions.reason: Untying a master's sandals was work for a slave. John counts himself lower still than the one to come (Luke 3:16).

decisions.choice: the Savior you are waiting for; someone greater
decisions.reason: Readable says who John meant, as the meaning note explains, and draws out the comparison the sandal saying makes.

records.source: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, υἱοὶ γένους Ἀβραὰμ καὶ οἱ ἐν ὑμῖν φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν, ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος τῆς σωτηρίας ταύτης ἐξαπεστάλη.
records.gloss: Men brothers, sons of [the] family of Abraham and those among you fearing God, to us the message of the salvation this has been sent.
pieces: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, {{gender:children|sons}} of Abraham's family, and you among us who fear God: this message of salvation has been sent out to us.

L.26: Men, brothers, sons of [the] family of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, to us the message of this salvation has been sent.

R.26: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you who belong to Abraham's family, and you others who worship God: God has sent this message of salvation to us!

decisions.choice: men, brothers: an address to fellow Jews, probably the whole congregation
decisions.reason: As in 13:16, Paul addresses the synagogue. The words alone cannot show whether the women present are included.

decisions.choice: those among you who fear God: the Gentile worshipers, as in 13:16
decisions.reason: Paul names the God-fearers alongside the descendants of Abraham: the message is for both.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to us"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "to you". Some early ones read "to us", which the SBLGNT prints. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: this message of salvation: the news that God has brought the Savior
decisions.reason: It looks back to the Savior Jesus (13:23).

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, children, with "brothers" and "sons" as the alternatives
decisions.reason: The inclusive default follows the meaning note; Literal keeps "men, brothers, sons".

records.source: οἱ γὰρ κατοικοῦντες ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες αὐτῶν τοῦτον ἀγνοήσαντες καὶ τὰς φωνὰς τῶν προφητῶν τὰς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκομένας κρίναντες ἐπλήρωσαν, καὶ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου εὑρόντες ᾐτήσαντο Πιλᾶτον ἀναιρεθῆναι αὐτόν·
records.gloss: Those for dwelling in Jerusalem and the rulers of them, him not having known and the voices of the prophets that on every Sabbath are being read, having condemned [him] they fulfilled [them], \v 28 and no cause of death having found they asked Pilate to put to death him;
pieces: The people of Jerusalem and their leaders did not know who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, and they did not understand the words of the prophets that are read out every Sabbath; yet by condemning {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} they made those words come true.
They found no charge that deserved death, and still they demanded that Pilate have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} killed.

L.27: For those who live in Jerusalem and their rulers, not recognizing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} or the voices of the prophets that are read every Sabbath, fulfilled [them] by condemning [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].
L.28: And though they found no cause for death, they asked Pilate that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be put to death.

R.27: The people who lived in Jerusalem and their leaders did not know who Jesus was. Every Sabbath they read the words of the prophets, but they did not understand them. They condemned Jesus to death, and by doing this they made the prophets' words come true.
R.28: They could not find any reason to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death. But they still asked Pilate to have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} killed.

decisions.choice: not recognizing him or the prophets: two things they failed to understand
alternatives: they did not know him, but knew the prophets
decisions.reason: The one verb governs both: they did not recognize Jesus or understand the prophets they heard each Sabbath.

decisions.choice: by condemning him they fulfilled them: their act carried out what the prophets had said
decisions.reason: As in 3:17-18: they acted in ignorance, and God fulfilled what he had foretold.

decisions.choice: the voices of the prophets: the words of the prophets
decisions.reason: Their writings are pictured as voices that speak whenever they are read.

decisions.choice: no cause of death: no charge that deserved death
decisions.reason: Pilate said as much (Luke 23:4, 23:14-15, 23:22).

decisions.choice: words
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps "voices".

records.source: ὡς δὲ ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένα, καθελόντες ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου ἔθηκαν εἰς μνημεῖον.
records.gloss: When then they had finished all the things about him having been written, having taken [him] down from the tree, they put [him] in a tomb.
pieces: When they had done everything that was written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down from the tree and laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a tomb.

L.29: And when they had carried out all the things written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they took [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] down from the tree and laid [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] in a tomb.

R.29: They did everything to Jesus that the Scriptures said would happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was taken down from the cross and put in a tomb.

decisions.choice: the tree: the cross, in the words of Deuteronomy 21:22-23
decisions.reason: The law spoke of one hanged on a tree as under God's curse (Deuteronomy 21:23; Galatians 3:13). Peter used the same word (5:30, 10:39).

decisions.choice: they took him down and laid him in a tomb: Paul speaks of the people of Jerusalem broadly, without naming who did it
alternatives: the same rulers who condemned him
decisions.reason: Paul speaks broadly. The Gospels say Joseph of Arimathea, a member of the council, took the body down and buried it (Luke 23:50-53).

decisions.choice: the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the tree was, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: he was taken down
decisions.reason: Readable uses a passive so as not to suggest that the rulers themselves buried him, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ὁ δὲ θεὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
records.gloss: But God raised him out from [the] dead,
pieces: But God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead,

decisions.choice: but God raised him: God reversed the verdict of men
decisions.reason: The same contrast runs through the speeches in Acts (2:23-24, 3:15, 4:10, 5:30).

decisions.choice: a comma, as the sentence goes on in 13:31
decisions.reason: The next verse begins with "who", so Literal and Balanced keep the sentence open; Readable ends it here.

records.source: ὃς ὤφθη ἐπὶ ἡμέρας πλείους τοῖς συναναβᾶσιν αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, οἵτινες νῦν εἰσὶ μάρτυρες αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν λαόν.
records.gloss: who appeared for days many to those having come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who now are witnesses of him to the people.
pieces: and for many days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appeared to those who had come up with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} witnesses to the people.

L.31: who appeared for many days to those who had come up with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} witnesses to the people.

R.31: For many days after that, Jesus appeared to the followers who had come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are telling the people of Israel about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: for many days: the forty days after the resurrection
decisions.reason: Luke says Jesus appeared to the apostles for forty days (1:3).

decisions.choice: who are now his witnesses: the Galilean followers, not Paul and Barnabas
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of the eyewitnesses who traveled with Jesus; he and Barnabas bring the good news (13:32).

decisions.choice: the people: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: In the speeches of Acts "the people" usually means Israel (13:17, 13:24).

decisions.choice: telling the people of Israel about him
decisions.reason: Readable says what being his witnesses means, and names the people, as the meaning notes explain.

records.source: καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελιζόμεθα τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίαν γενομένην ὅτι ταύτην ὁ θεὸς ἐκπεπλήρωκεν τοῖς τέκνοις ἡμῶν ἀναστήσας Ἰησοῦν, ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ γέγραπται τῷ δευτέρῳ· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε.
records.gloss: And we to you preach the good news, the to the fathers promise having been made, \v 33 that this God has fulfilled to the children of us, having raised up Jesus, as also in the psalm it has been written the second, Son of me are you, I today have begotten you.
pieces: And we are bringing you good news: the promise made to the {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}
God has now fulfilled for our children by raising up Jesus. So it stands written in the second psalm: 'You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son; today I have begotten {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

L.32: And we bring you the good news [of] the promise made to the fathers,
L.33: that God has fulfilled this to our children by raising up Jesus, as it is also written in the second psalm, 'You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son; today I have begotten {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

R.32: We are telling you the good news about what God promised our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.
R.33: God has now done what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised, for our children, by raising up Jesus. This is what is written in the second psalm: 'You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son. Today I have become {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Father.'

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to our children"
decisions.reason: The best early manuscripts read "to our children", which the SBLGNT prints although it reads awkwardly. Many later manuscripts have "to us, their children", which fits Paul's point more smoothly. On the SBLGNT reading Paul speaks as one of the people of Israel and means the present generation, the descendants of the fathers. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: raising up Jesus: either bringing him on the scene, or raising him from the dead
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God raising up a prophet or king (3:22, 7:37) and of the resurrection (2:24, 2:32). Verse 34 goes on to speak of raising him "from the dead", which may mean 13:33 is about sending him, or that 13:34 adds the point that he will never die again.

decisions.choice: Psalm 2:7, God's words to the king he has installed
decisions.reason: In Psalm 2 God says these words to the king on the day he sets him on his throne. Paul applies them to Jesus. Codex Bezae reads "the first psalm", from a time when Psalms 1 and 2 were sometimes counted as one; reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: today I have begotten you: today I have made you my son, my king
decisions.reason: In the psalm the "today" is the day the king takes his throne. Paul links the words to the resurrection, as Romans 1:4 links Jesus's being shown to be Son of God with his rising.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means forebears; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: Today I have become your Father
decisions.reason: "Begotten" is not an everyday word; Readable says the same thing in plain words.

records.source: ὅτι δὲ ἀνέστησεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν μηκέτι μέλλοντα ὑποστρέφειν εἰς διαφθοράν, οὕτως εἴρηκεν ὅτι Δώσω ὑμῖν τὰ ὅσια Δαυὶδ τὰ πιστά.
records.gloss: That then he raised him out from [the] dead, no more being about to return to decay, thus he has spoken that, I will give to you the holy [things] of David, the sure [things].
pieces: And that God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead, never again to go back to decay, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} declared in these words: 'I will give you the holy blessings of David, the ones that can be trusted.'

L.34: And that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from [the] dead, no longer about to return to decay, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken thus: 'I will give you the holy [things] of David, the sure [things].'

R.34: God raised Jesus from death, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body will never decay. God had said this would happen, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'I will give you the holy blessings that I promised to David, and you can trust that I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promises.'

decisions.choice: Isaiah 55:3, in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: God promises his people the faithful love he showed to David. The Hebrew reads "the sure mercies of David"; the Greek has "the holy things of David, the sure things".

decisions.choice: the holy things of David, the sure things: the blessings God promised David, which he faithfully keeps
decisions.reason: The plural words mean holy and trustworthy blessings. The word for "holy" is the same root as "Holy One" in the next quotation (13:35), which is why Paul sets the two side by side.

decisions.choice: never to return to decay: never to die again
decisions.reason: Jesus did not decay in the grave (13:37). "Return" means he will never again go back to death.

decisions.choice: you: plural, God's people
decisions.reason: The "you" is plural. The blessings promised to David come to the people through the one God raised.

decisions.choice: three sentences, with the promise explained
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence and says what the holy and sure things are, as the meaning notes explain.

records.source: διότι καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει· Οὐ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν·
records.gloss: Therefore also in another he says, Not you will allow the Holy One of you to see decay.
pieces: That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also says in another psalm, 'You will not let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy One undergo decay.'

L.35: Therefore {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also says in another [psalm], 'You will not allow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy One to see decay.'

R.35: In another psalm God also says, 'You will not let the body of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy One rot.'

decisions.choice: Psalm 16:10, as Peter quoted it in 2:27
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament has "decay" where the Hebrew may mean "the pit". Paul's argument, like Peter's, rests on the word decay.

decisions.choice: he says: God speaks in the Scripture
decisions.reason: The psalm is David's, but Paul treats it as God's word; "he" carries on from God in 13:34.

decisions.choice: your Holy One: the one devoted and faithful to God
decisions.reason: The word is the same root as "holy things" in 13:34. As at 2:27, it points to the Messiah.

decisions.choice: the body of ... rot
decisions.reason: Readable says what decay means here, as at 2:27.

records.source: Δαυὶδ μὲν γὰρ ἰδίᾳ γενεᾷ ὑπηρετήσας τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ βουλῇ ἐκοιμήθη καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶδεν διαφθοράν, ὃν δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν οὐκ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.
records.gloss: David indeed for in his own generation having served the of God purpose fell asleep and was added to the fathers of him and saw decay; \v 37 the [one] however God raised up not did see decay.
pieces: For David, after serving God's purpose in his own generation, fell asleep in death; he was laid to rest with his {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, and his body decayed.
But the one whom God raised up did not undergo decay.

L.36: For David, having served the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep and was laid with his fathers and saw decay;
L.37: but the one whom God raised up did not see decay.

R.36: David did what God wanted him to do while he was alive. Then he died. He was buried with his {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, and his body rotted away.
R.37: But God raised Jesus to life, and the body of Jesus did not rot.

decisions.choice: served God's purpose in his own generation
alternatives: served his own generation, and by God's purpose fell asleep
decisions.reason: "God's purpose" can go with "served" or with "fell asleep". Taking it with "served" gives the plainer sense: David did God's will in his lifetime.

decisions.choice: fell asleep: died
decisions.reason: A common biblical way of speaking of death, as of Stephen (7:60).

decisions.choice: was added to his fathers: was buried and joined his forebears in death
decisions.reason: A phrase from the Old Testament (Judges 2:10; 1 Kings 2:10).

decisions.choice: David decayed, Jesus did not: so the psalm speaks of Jesus
decisions.reason: The same argument as Peter's in 2:29-31.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means forebears; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: Jesus
alternatives: the one whom God raised up
decisions.reason: Readable names the one Paul means.

records.source: γνωστὸν οὖν ἔστω ὑμῖν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὅτι διὰ τούτου ὑμῖν ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν καταγγέλλεται, καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων ὧν οὐκ ἠδυνήθητε ἐν νόμῳ Μωϋσέως δικαιωθῆναι ἐν τούτῳ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων δικαιοῦται.
records.gloss: Known therefore be it to you, men brothers, that through this [one] to you forgiveness of sins is proclaimed, and from all things from which not you were able in [the] law of Moses to be justified, \v 39 in this [one] everyone who believes is justified.
pieces: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you must know this: through this man forgiveness of sins is being announced to you, and from everything the law of Moses could not acquit you of,
everyone who believes is acquitted through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.38: Therefore let it be known to you, men, brothers, that through this [one] forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you, and from all [the things] from which you could not be justified by [the] law of Moses,
L.39: by this [one] everyone who believes is justified.

R.38: So, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I want you to know this: we are telling you that God forgives your sins because of what Jesus has done. You could not be freed from your guilt by keeping the law of Moses.
R.39: But everyone who believes in Jesus is made right with God and freed from all of it.

decisions.choice: men, brothers: as in 13:26, the whole congregation
decisions.reason: Paul repeats the address of 13:26.

decisions.choice: justified from: acquitted of, set free from the guilt of
decisions.reason: With "from", the verb is a legal word: to be declared free of the charges against one. It is the verb Paul uses for being set right with God (Romans 3:24, 3:28; Galatians 2:16). It is not the noun "righteousness".

decisions.choice: the law could never acquit; believing in Jesus does
alternatives: the law acquits of some things, Jesus of the rest
decisions.reason: The words could be read as if the law acquitted of some sins and Jesus of the others. Paul's point is that the law could not do it, and faith in Jesus does it fully (Galatians 2:16).

decisions.choice: by this one: through Jesus
decisions.reason: "This one" points back to Jesus, as at the start of 13:38.

decisions.choice: acquit, acquitted
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain legal word for the legal sense, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps "justified".

decisions.choice: freed from your guilt; made right with God and freed
decisions.reason: Readable says what being justified means, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative; Literal keeps "men, brothers"
decisions.reason: As at 13:26.

records.source: βλέπετε οὖν μὴ ἐπέλθῃ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις·
records.gloss: Take heed therefore lest might come about the [thing] having been said in the prophets,
pieces: So be careful, or what was said in the Prophets may come upon you:

L.40: Watch out, therefore, so that what has been said in the Prophets does not come upon [you]:

R.40: So be careful! Do not let the words of the prophets come true about you. They said,

decisions.choice: in the prophets: in the books of the Prophets
decisions.reason: The quotation comes from Habakkuk, one of the twelve shorter prophetic books, which were counted together.

decisions.choice: lest it come: a warning that it may come upon them
decisions.reason: Paul warns that the words could be fulfilled in them.

decisions.choice: two sentences, and "They said"
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the warning and leads into the quotation.

records.source: Ἴδετε, οἱ καταφρονηταί, καὶ θαυμάσατε καὶ ἀφανίσθητε, ὅτι ἔργον ἐργάζομαι ἐγὼ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ὑμῶν, ἔργον ὃ οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε ἐάν τις ἐκδιηγῆται ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: Behold, the scoffers, and wonder and perish, because a work am working I in the days of you, a work which never not you would believe if someone should declare it to you.
pieces: 'See, you who scorn, be astonished and vanish! For I am doing a work in your days, a work you would never believe, even if someone explained it to you.'"

L.41: 'Look, you scoffers, and wonder, and perish, for I am working a work in your days, a work that you will never believe, even if someone tells you in full.'"

R.41: 'Look, you people who laugh at God! Be amazed and die! I am doing something in your lifetime that you will not believe, even if someone tells you about it.'"

decisions.choice: Habakkuk 1:5, in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "Look among the nations"; the Greek has "Look, you scoffers". In Habakkuk the astonishing work was God bringing the Babylonians in judgment. Paul applies the warning to those who reject God's work in Jesus.

decisions.choice: perish: vanish, be destroyed
decisions.reason: The verb means to disappear or be destroyed.

decisions.choice: you will never believe: a strong denial
decisions.reason: The two negatives make it emphatic.

decisions.choice: you people who laugh at God
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what scoffers do.

records.source: Ἐξιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν παρεκάλουν εἰς τὸ μεταξὺ σάββατον λαληθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα.
records.gloss: Going out then they, they were begging on the next Sabbath to be spoken to them the words these.
pieces: As Paul and Barnabas were going out, the people kept urging them to speak about these things again on the next Sabbath.

L.42: And as they were going out, they were begging that these words be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.

R.42: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to come back the next Sabbath and tell them more about these things.

decisions.choice: they were going out; the people were begging
decisions.reason: The Greek does not name either group. Those leaving are most naturally Paul and Barnabas; those who ask are the people of the synagogue.

decisions.choice: the next Sabbath
decisions.reason: The word can mean "between" or "next". 13:44 shows the next Sabbath is meant.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "as they were going out, they were begging"
alternatives: "as the Jews were going out of the synagogue, the Gentiles begged"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, name the Jews as leaving and the Gentiles as asking. The earlier manuscripts name neither. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Paul and Barnabas; the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two groups, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: λυθείσης δὲ τῆς συναγωγῆς ἠκολούθησαν πολλοὶ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ τῶν σεβομένων προσηλύτων τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρναβᾷ, οἵτινες προσλαλοῦντες αὐτοῖς ἔπειθον· αὐτοὺς προσμένειν τῇ χάριτι τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Having broken up then the synagogue, followed many of the Jews and of the worshiping converts Paul and Barnabas, who speaking to them were persuading them to continue in the grace of God.
pieces: After the gathering broke up, many Jews and converts who worshiped God went along with Paul and Barnabas, who talked with them and kept persuading them to remain in the grace of God.

L.43: And when the synagogue [meeting] had broken up, many of the Jews and of the worshiping proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking to them, were urging them to continue in the grace of God.

R.43: When the meeting was over, many Jews followed Paul and Barnabas. So did many Gentiles who had become Jews and worshiped God. Paul and Barnabas talked with them and urged them to keep on trusting in the grace of God.

decisions.choice: worshiping proselytes: Gentiles who had become Jews by conversion
decisions.reason: A proselyte was a Gentile who took on the law of Moses in full (2:10, 6:5). Luke here joins the word with "worshiping", which he elsewhere uses of the God-fearers (16:14, 17:4); the line between the groups may not be sharp.

decisions.choice: continue in the grace of God: keep relying on God's kindness that they had now received
decisions.reason: The grace of God is his undeserved kindness in Jesus, which they had welcomed in the message (11:23, 14:3).

decisions.choice: who: Paul and Barnabas, urging the people
alternatives: the people urging Paul and Barnabas
decisions.reason: The nearer names are Paul and Barnabas, and the urging to continue in grace fits them.

decisions.choice: Gentiles who had become Jews; keep on trusting in
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word proselyte and what continuing in grace means, as the meaning notes explain.

records.source: Τῷ δὲ ἐρχομένῳ σαββάτῳ σχεδὸν πᾶσα ἡ πόλις συνήχθη ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου.
records.gloss: On the now coming Sabbath almost all the city was gathered together to hear the word of the Lord.
pieces: The following Sabbath nearly the entire city came together to hear the word of the Lord.

L.44: And on the coming Sabbath almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of the Lord.

R.44: On the next Sabbath almost everyone in the city came to hear the word of the Lord.

decisions.choice: almost the whole city: a great crowd, Jews and Gentiles alike
decisions.reason: The crowds in 13:45 and the Gentiles in 13:48 show that many beyond the synagogue came.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the word of the Lord"
decisions.reason: Some important manuscripts read "the word of God". The meaning is much the same. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

records.heading: The whole city gathers to hear

records.source: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τοὺς ὄχλους ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου καὶ ἀντέλεγον τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λαλουμένοις βλασφημοῦντες.
records.gloss: Having seen however the Jews the crowds were filled with jealousy and were contradicting the things by Paul being spoken, blaspheming.
pieces: But when the Jews saw the crowds, jealousy filled them, and they spoke against what Paul was saying and reviled him.

L.45: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and began contradicting the things spoken by Paul, blaspheming.

R.45: But when the Jews there saw all those people, they became jealous. They argued against what Paul was saying, and they said terrible things about him.

decisions.choice: blaspheming: speaking abusively, against Paul and his message
decisions.reason: The word means to slander or revile. Because the message is about Jesus, reviling it may also be speaking against God, as Luke implies (18:6, 26:11).

decisions.choice: jealousy: resentment at the crowds drawn to Paul
decisions.reason: The word can mean zeal or jealousy. Seeing the crowds is what provokes it, as in 5:17.

decisions.choice: the Jews: those Jews of the synagogue who opposed Paul
decisions.reason: Many Jews had followed Paul gladly (13:43). Luke means those who now opposed him.

decisions.choice: reviled him
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the meaning chosen; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: the Jews there
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the Jews of that synagogue are meant, not all Jews, as the meaning note explains. It does not narrow them to the leaders, which the Greek does not say.

records.source: παρρησιασάμενοί τε ὁ Παῦλος καὶ ὁ Βαρναβᾶς εἶπαν· Ὑμῖν ἦν ἀναγκαῖον πρῶτον λαληθῆναι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ· ἐπειδὴ ἀπωθεῖσθε αὐτὸν καὶ οὐκ ἀξίους κρίνετε ἑαυτοὺς τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς, ἰδοὺ στρεφόμεθα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη·
records.gloss: Having spoken boldly also Paul and Barnabas said, To you it was necessary first to be spoken the word of God; since you thrust away it and not worthy judge yourselves of the eternal life, behold, we are turning to the Gentiles.
pieces: Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly: "The word of God had to be spoken to you first. Since you push it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, see, we are turning to the Gentiles.

L.46: And Paul and Barnabas, speaking boldly, said, "It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first. Since you thrust it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look, we are turning to the Gentiles.

R.46: Then Paul and Barnabas spoke bravely. They said, "We had to tell God's message to you Jews first. But you refuse to listen. You are showing that you do not think you are good enough for eternal life. So now we will go to the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: to you first: God's word was to come first to Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus sent his witnesses starting from Jerusalem (1:8; Luke 24:47), and Paul writes "to the Jew first" (Romans 1:16). Paul keeps going first to the synagogue after this (14:1, 17:1-2).

decisions.choice: you judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life: by your own choice you show you will not have it
decisions.reason: Paul says their rejection is their own verdict on themselves.

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: As in 13:48, life with God that does not end.

decisions.choice: we are turning to the Gentiles: in this city
alternatives: they will never again preach to Jews
decisions.reason: In the next town they go first to the synagogue again (14:1).

decisions.choice: you Jews
decisions.reason: Readable names the hearers, who are the Jews of 13:45.

decisions.choice: you are showing that you do not think you are good enough
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: οὕτως γὰρ ἐντέταλται ἡμῖν ὁ κύριος· Τέθεικά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν τοῦ εἶναί σε εἰς σωτηρίαν ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: Thus for has commanded us the Lord, I have set you for a light of nations, to be you for salvation to [the] end of the earth.
pieces: For this is the command the Lord has given us: 'I have set you as a light for the nations, so that you may be the means of salvation to the farthest part of the earth.'"

L.47: For thus the Lord has commanded us: 'I have set you as a light for [the] nations, that you may be for salvation to [the] end of the earth.'"

R.47: This is what the Lord told us to do when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'I have made you a light for the nations. You will bring salvation to people all over the earth.'"

decisions.choice: Isaiah 49:6, God's words to his servant
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the LORD, the divine name in the Hebrew, speaks to his servant. Simeon applied the words to Jesus (Luke 2:32). Here Paul and Barnabas take them as their own commission, since they carry the servant's light to the nations.

decisions.choice: nations: the peoples of the world, the Gentiles
decisions.reason: The same word is "Gentiles" in 13:46 and 13:48. In the quotation it keeps the sense of all the peoples.

decisions.choice: you: singular, the servant of the Lord
decisions.reason: The "you" is singular in Isaiah, and Paul and Barnabas say the Lord commanded "us".

decisions.choice: the end of the earth: the whole world
decisions.reason: The same words as Jesus's commission in 1:8.

decisions.choice: you will bring salvation to people all over the earth
alternatives: to be for salvation to the end of the earth
decisions.reason: Readable says the purpose in plain words.

records.source: ἀκούοντα δὲ τὰ ἔθνη ἔχαιρον καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν ὅσοι ἦσαν τεταγμένοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον·
records.gloss: Hearing [it] then the Gentiles were rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, and believed as many as were appointed to life eternal;
pieces: When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who had been appointed to eternal life believed.

L.48: And when the Gentiles heard [this], they were rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, and as many as were appointed to eternal life believed.

R.48: The Gentiles were very happy when they heard this. They glorified the Lord for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word. And all the people God had chosen for eternal life believed.

decisions.choice: were appointed: a passive, appointed by God
alternatives: had set themselves toward eternal life
decisions.reason: The form is most naturally passive, and the one who appoints to eternal life is God. A middle sense, "had set themselves", has been proposed but is not the natural reading of the form.

decisions.choice: God's appointing and their believing go together
decisions.reason: Luke states that those appointed believed, without explaining how God's appointing and human believing relate. Paul has just urged his hearers to believe (13:39-41), and the Jews who refused judged themselves unworthy (13:46).

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: The same phrase as in 13:46.

decisions.choice: glorifying the word of the Lord: praising God for the message
decisions.reason: They honored the message by praising God for it.

decisions.choice: the people God had chosen
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who appoints, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: glorified the Lord for his word
alternatives: glorifying the word of the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says what glorifying the word means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: διεφέρετο δὲ ὁ λόγος τοῦ κυρίου δι’ ὅλης τῆς χώρας.
records.gloss: Was carried through then the word of the Lord through all the region.
pieces: And the word of the Lord spread across the whole region.

L.49: And the word of the Lord was being carried through the whole region.

R.49: The word of the Lord spread to all the places around that city.

decisions.choice: the region: the country around Pisidian Antioch
decisions.reason: The city was the center of a wider district (13:50).

decisions.choice: was being carried: the message kept spreading
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures an ongoing spread, as in 6:7 and 12:24.

records.source: οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι παρώτρυναν τὰς σεβομένας γυναῖκας τὰς εὐσχήμονας καὶ τοὺς πρώτους τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἐπήγειραν διωγμὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρναβᾶν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: The but Jews incited the worshiping women of honorable position and the leading [men] of the city, and they stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and expelled them from the district of them.
pieces: But the Jews stirred up the respected women who worshiped God and the leading men of the city; they started a persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district.

L.50: But the Jews incited the worshiping women of high standing and the leading [men] of the city, and stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and threw them out of their district.

R.50: But the Jews there stirred up some important women who worshiped God. They also stirred up the leaders of the city. These people began to make trouble for Paul and Barnabas, and they forced them to leave the area.

decisions.choice: worshiping women of high standing: Gentile women of rank who attended the synagogue
decisions.reason: The word "worshiping" is used of Gentiles who worshiped Israel's God (16:14, 17:4). Such women could have influence with the leading men, perhaps their husbands.

decisions.choice: the leading men of the city: its chief citizens and officials
decisions.reason: The word means the first or most prominent men. Antioch was a Roman colony run by local magistrates.

decisions.choice: threw them out of their district: forced them to leave the city's territory
decisions.reason: The verb means to drive or throw out. Paul later came back to the city (14:21).

decisions.choice: the Jews there
decisions.reason: As at 13:45: the Jews of that city's synagogue, not all Jews.

decisions.choice: three sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence up.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐκτιναξάμενοι τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἦλθον εἰς Ἰκόνιον, οἵ τε μαθηταὶ ἐπληροῦντο χαρᾶς καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου.
records.gloss: They but having shaken off the dust of the feet against them went to Iconium, \v 52 the and disciples were filled with joy and with [the] Holy Spirit.
pieces: So the two shook the dust from their feet against them and went on to Iconium.
And the disciples went on being filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

L.51: But they, having shaken off the dust of [their] feet against them, went to Iconium,
L.52: and the disciples were being filled with joy and with [the] Holy Spirit.

R.51: So Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet to warn the people who had rejected them. Then they went to the city of Iconium.
R.52: But the believers in Antioch were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: shaking off the dust against them: a sign of leaving them to answer for their choice
decisions.reason: Jesus told his messengers to do this when a town would not receive them (Luke 9:5, 10:11). It was a warning, not a curse.

decisions.choice: the disciples: the new believers in Antioch
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas have just left. Luke turns to those who remained, who were glad in spite of the persecution.

decisions.choice: were being filled: kept on being filled
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures an ongoing state.

decisions.choice: Iconium: a city about ninety miles east of Pisidian Antioch
decisions.reason: It lay on the main road east, in the province of Galatia. Paul's work there is told in 14:1-6.

decisions.choice: to warn the people who had rejected them; the believers in Antioch
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sign meant and who the disciples were, as the meaning notes explain.
